title: First 30d Acceleration Sprint and Evidence Rubric
body:
Purpose:
This is a practical playbook for accelerating new hires to early impact in the first 30 days. It combines a lightweight hiring-evidence rubric (to be used by interviewers and onboarding partners) with an actionable day-by-day induction sprint and an exit-readiness checklist for managers. Aim: shorten time-to-customer-impact while keeping hiring signal and experience high.

Context and assumptions:
- For ICs (IC2-IC4) across Eng/Product/Platform, with lightweight variants for non-engineering roles.
- Not replacing role-specific onboarding decks; this is a focused acceleration overlay (30-day sprint) that sits on top of role materials.
- Interview evidence rubric below is intentionally short (3–5 competencies) to keep interviewer calibration consistent.

Success metrics (first 30d):
- Week 2: can run local dev or sandbox workflow end-to-end (PR, run, test) OR produce a domain artifact (spec, customer investigation) depending on role.
- Week 4: first independently-owned small deliverable shipped or handed off to partner (measured by PR merged / task closed).
- Manager satisfaction: >= "meets expectations" on the 30-day signoff template.
- New hire self-report: >= 4/5 on clarity of priorities and ramp progress.

Sprint calendar (high level):
- Preboarding (before day 0): IT access checklist, repo clone + smoke test, reading list (3 docs), calendar invites for mentor and onboarding syncs.
- Week 1 (days 0–5): orientation + sandbox tasks. Daily 30m sync with mentor. Goal: environment working, first read/annotate of 2 core docs, complete a tiny end-to-end task.
- Week 2 (days 6–12): pairing and context deep dive. Take ownership of a small bug or doc. First 1:1 with manager sets 30-day priorities and success criteria.
- Week 3 (days 13–19): independent work on a small deliverable; ramp meeting with cross-functional partner. Draft a short postmortem or spec fragment.
- Week 4 (days 20–30): ship deliverable, 30-day review prep, clear next-90d objectives. Manager runs signoff checklist and schedules development plan discussion.

Day-by-day sample micro-plan (engineering IC):
- Day -3 to 0: access granted, clone core repo, run test suite smoke. Slack intro, add to #team channel, book 1:1s.
- Day 0: orientation (HR), security training, team kickoff (30m), mentor pairing starts.
- Day 1: local dev environment; run hello-world example; tiny bug assigned (should compile/run).
- Day 2: pair with mentor to extend tiny bug, create PR draft.
- Day 3: finish PR, ship to staging, write 1-paragraph summary of approach in ticket.
- Day 4: feedback loop from reviewer, iterate.
- Day 5: retro w/ mentor: what blocked you, what was surprising.
- Week 2–3: ramp tasks scale in size; first independent task that touches infra or model config.
- Week 4: ship, document, and present short demo to team.

Hiring & interview evidence rubric (compact):
Competencies (core five):
- Technical problem solving (TP): ability to decompose and propose pragmatic solutions.
- Execution and ownership (EO): follow-through and delivery bias.
- Communication & cross-team collaboration (CC): clarity with stakeholders and ability to surface tradeoffs.
- Learning velocity (LV): ability to absorb new infra/domain and apply quickly.
- Reliability & judgement (RJ): risk-awareness, test coverage, and sensible defaults.

Scoring guidance (1–5) — use whole numbers only:
- 5 = Exceptional: clear, repeatable examples of end-to-end ownership and strong tradeoff reasoning.
- 4 = Strong: consistent examples, minor gaps in edge cases.
- 3 = Solid: meets baseline, needs some ramping but will reach independence quickly.
- 2 = Weak: missing key examples; would need close mentoring.
- 1 = Not demonstrated: lacks evidence for competency.

Interview probes mapped to evidence examples (example prompts):
- TP: "Describe a time you diagnosed a perf regression in production." Evidence: steps to isolate, controlled experiments, rollback plan.
- EO: "Tell me about a small project you shipped start-to-finish." Evidence: milestones, handling blockers, post-launch followup.
- CC: "How did you coordinate with PM/infra on a feature?" Evidence: meeting cadence, artifact handoff, documented decisions.
- LV: "What new stack did you learn recently? How did you onboard yourself?" Evidence: reading plan, checkpoints, early contributions.
- RJ: "Give an example where you chose not to ship a change; why?" Evidence: risk analysis, rollback strategy, monitoring plan.

Interviewer checklist (quick):
- Capture 1–2 concrete examples per competency.
- Rate 1–5 and add 1–2 sentence justification.
- Signal: hire / hire-with-concerns / no-hire. If hire-with-concerns, specify top 2 onboarding mitigations.

Manager 30-day signoff checklist (Exit-readiness):
- Environment & access: dev + infra access confirmed (yes/no).
- Sandbox task: completed and reviewed by mentor (yes/no).
- Deliverable: scoped and shipped OR clear owner handoff (yes/no).
- Evidence: interview-rubric competencies re-assessed from onboarding artifacts (manager notes) and align with hire decision.
- Development plan: 90-day objectives set and shared in calendar (yes/no).
- Peer check: at least 2 peers can explain the new hire's scope and dependencies (yes/no).
- Final rating (manager): "On track" / "Needs support" / "Mis-hire" plus free-text.

Onboarding mitigations and common playbook patches (if scoring gaps):
- LV gap: schedule focused learning sprints with reading list + mentor checkpoints; pair daily first week.
- EO gap: assign a micro-owner task with explicit acceptance criteria and weekly check-ins.
- CC gap: schedule stakeholder shadowing sessions and require a short cross-team writeup.

Manager & mentor responsibilities (short):
- Manager: define 3 clear 30-day outcomes and book weekly 1:1s; remove blockers; provide clear acceptance criteria.
- Mentor: daily quick sync (15–30m) first week, code pairing, review PRs in <48h, escalate blocking infra tickets immediately.

Preboarding checklist (to be auto-run by PeopleOps before day 0):
- Hardware ordered + shipped, accounts provisioned (OKTA, GH, Google), Slack + calendar invites, reading list link, mentor assigned, first-week meetings scheduled.

Templates included (links/IDs):
- 30-day manager signoff template (linked artifact above).
- Interview scorecard quick form (JIRA-OPS-1243).

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Should we formalize a variant of this sprint for non-engineering roles? (ops: Leah to draft).
- Can we instrument "first-PR-to-merged" time automatically for ramp metric? (eng: Marco to file infra ticket).
- Decide minimal paired-hours expectation for mentors (proposal: 6hrs first week).

Notes to self (working):
- Keep rubric short — too many competencies dilutes signal.
- Consolidate onboarding reading lists per role and attach to this doc.
- Try a pilot with 6 hires this quarter and measure time-to-first-merged-pr and manager satisfaction.

Action items (owners):
- Marco: create infra ticket to capture first-PR metric (due 2026-02-05).
- Leah: draft non-engineering variant and share by 2026-02-12.
- Dylan: add interview scorecard quick form to the panel booking flow (due 2026-02-08).
